$comment: Keyword-to-page map for the published archive. One primary intent per page; no two pages may claim the same primary keyword. `evidence` records what was actually observed during research (search results, CryptoHack solve counts on 2026-11-26) - no search volumes are asserted because none were measured.

pages.intent: navigational: find the site behind the Radiant Blaze name
pages.evidence: Brand term; no competing site uses the name.

pages.intent: informational: browse short technical notes
pages.evidence: Generic category term; broad and competitive, so the page targets the browse intent rather than a single post.

pages.intent: informational: browse writeups grouped by competition
pages.evidence: Observed aggregator pages (CTFtime, team blogs) compete for generic 'ctf writeups'; the event grouping is the differentiator.

pages.intent: navigational: find the author's work
pages.evidence: Name-based query; matches the portfolio's own display name.

pages.intent: navigational/informational: the project file for this site
pages.evidence: Brand + project page; no external competition observed.

pages.intent: informational: keep a static Astro build while adding SPA-like navigation
pages.evidence: Build log for this site; targets the architecture intent rather than a generic Astro tutorial query.

pages.intent: informational: derive topic, feed, and social-card layers from static content
pages.evidence: Build log for the generated topic/feed layer; no external competition observed for the combined intent.

pages.intent: informational: practical terminal workflow
pages.evidence: Long-tail; generic 'linux aliases' is saturated by listicles, so the note targets the narrower toolkit framing.

pages.intent: informational: solve a specific course challenge
pages.evidence: CryptoHack reports 98,485 solves and 2 official solutions; many independent blogs publish writeups, so competition is high and the exact-name query is the viable entry point.

pages.intent: informational: decode ASCII codes
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; several multi-challenge blog posts cover it as one section.

pages.intent: informational: decode hex to bytes
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; independent writeups observed.

pages.intent: informational: hex to bytes to Base64
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; usually covered inside multi-challenge posts.

pages.primary: cryptohack bytes and big integers writeup
pages.intent: informational: convert an integer back to bytes
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; the Windows import detail is a distinct long-tail angle.

pages.intent: informational: first XOR exercise
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; covered inside CryptoHack series posts.

pages.intent: informational: undo chained XOR
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; fewer dedicated writeups than the starter challenge.

pages.intent: informational: brute-force a one-byte XOR key
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; the brute-force angle overlaps many general single-byte-XOR tutorials.

pages.primary: cryptohack you either know xor you dont writeup
pages.intent: informational: known-plaintext key recovery
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; the challenge name is distinctive enough for an exact-query match.

pages.intent: informational: gcd of two integers
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; a Chinese-language series was the main competing writeup observed.

pages.intent: informational: extended Euclidean algorithm
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; competing writeups often only show the SymPy call.

pages.intent: informational: basic modular reduction
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; covered as a section in series posts.

pages.intent: informational: prime-modulus exponentiation
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; Fermat's Little Theorem is a well-covered general topic.

pages.intent: informational: multiplicative inverse
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; the three-argument pow() one-liner is the distinctive detail.

pages.intent: informational: identify residues by brute force
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; usually grouped inside modular-arithmetic series posts.

pages.intent: informational: classify residues for a large prime
pages.evidence: CryptoHack reports 16,895 solves and 55 official solutions - high competition, so the exact challenge-name query is the target.

pages.intent: informational: extract a modular square root
pages.evidence: CryptoHack reports 15,267 solves and 51 official solutions; competing writeups often stop at the SageMath one-liner.

pages.intent: informational: solve simultaneous congruences
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; CRT is a common textbook topic with broad competition.

pages.intent: informational: decode a Goldwasser-Micali style ciphertext
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; the challenge name is distinctive.

pages.intent: informational: recover RSA primes from linear combinations
pages.evidence: Course challenge page exists; RSA factor-recovery searches are competitive but usually target generic attacks.

pages.intent: informational: solve a specific competition challenge
pages.evidence: Observed competitor writeups: cybersecurityelite.com ASIS 2026 crypto roundup, a 28-challenge GitHub repo, and a Magichrist archive page.

pages.intent: informational: solve the nonlinear-oracle crypto challenge
pages.evidence: Competitor coverage appears inside multi-challenge ASIS 2026 roundups rather than dedicated pages.

pages.primary: digital pakistan red team ctf helios vault
pages.intent: informational: solve the threshold-sharing challenge
pages.evidence: No dedicated public writeup surfaced for this event's challenges during the search; the event name plus challenge is the long-tail target.

pages.primary: digital pakistan red team ctf spec warden
pages.intent: informational: solve the OpenAPI validation bypass
pages.evidence: No dedicated public writeup surfaced; target the exact challenge name.

pages.primary: digital pakistan red team ctf promise
pages.intent: informational: solve the continued-fractions KEM
pages.evidence: No dedicated public writeup surfaced; exact-name query only.

pages.primary: digital pakistan red team ctf meeeps

pages.evidence: No dedicated public writeup surfaced; MIPS pwn content is rare, which favours the long-tail query.

pages.primary: digital pakistan red team ctf hoe ap
pages.intent: informational: solve the handle-only heap challenge
pages.evidence: No dedicated public writeup surfaced; the challenge name is the only realistic query.

gaps.reason: The existing toolkit post is the only Linux note and is short; a dedicated note with verified command examples would be required before targeting this query.
The site itself is built on this stack, but no article documents it yet; writing one requires a separate, researched piece.
Would need a curated guide that does not exist; do not fake it.
